companies.name: Soracom
companies.description: Soracom is a global IoT cellular connectivity and platform provider headquartered in Tokyo, founded in 2014, with regional operations in the US (Soracom Global) and EU. The platform pairs multicarrier SIMs (physical, eSIM, iSIM) across 170+ countries with a deep platform of cloud integration services (Beam, Funnel, Funk), data services (Harvest, Lagoon, Query, Orbit), device management (Inventory, Krypton, Endorse, Napter), and network gateways (VPG / Canal / Direct / Door / Gate / Junction / Peek). Soracom exposes the entire stack through a coverage-aware REST API documented at users.soracom.io and maintained as a public OpenAPI 3.0 specification in the soracom-cli GitHub repo.

companies.name: KUFU
companies.description: KUFU, Inc. is the founding name of SmartHR, Inc., the Japanese cloud HR platform, and remains the company's GitHub organization identity. SmartHR is a system of record for employee data across Japanese back-office HR — hiring and onboarding, social insurance and labour paperwork, family and dependent records, organizational structure, payslips, and withholding tax slips. The SmartHR API is a tenant-scoped REST API on a per-customer subdomain, described by a live Swagger 2.0 document covering 60 paths and 120 operations, and is offered free to existing SmartHR customers. It ships a webhook event surface, an application-gated sandbox on a separate domain, and an open-source React component library, but no official client SDK.

companies.name: Paidy
companies.description: Paidy is a Japanese buy now, pay later (BNPL) and digital payment service that enables Japanese consumers to make purchases and pay later via monthly consolidated billing. Merchants integrate Paidy Checkout (JavaScript) and the Paidy REST API to accept deferred payments, manage authorizations, capture funds, issue refunds, and handle recurring payments via stored tokens.

companies.name: Logiless
companies.description: LOGILESS (ロジレス) is a Japanese cloud EC logistics platform that unifies order management (OMS) and warehouse management (WMS) for e-commerce merchants — automating order intake from marketplaces and shopping carts (Rakuten, Shopify, ColorMe, futureshop, ec-force and more), inventory synchronization, allocation, shipping-label issuance and warehouse operations. LOGILESS exposes a RESTful, OAuth2-protected API (scoped per merchant) for reading and writing sales orders, outbound and inbound deliveries, sales returns, inter-warehouse transfers, articles (product master), multi-layer inventory summaries, warehouses, stores and suppliers. The company is a 500 Global portfolio company. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from LOGILESS's public developer documentation; the OpenAPI here is derived and not an official LOGILESS artifact.

companies.name: PayPay
companies.description: PayPay is Japan's largest QR/barcode mobile-payment network (a SoftBank / Yahoo Japan / Paytm joint venture) with tens of millions of users. Its Open Payment API (OPA v2) lets payment partners and merchants collect payments from PayPay wallet users through dynamic QR codes, web checkout (Web Cashier), app-invoke deep links, and a pre-authorize-and-capture flow. The REST API (base //apigw.paypay.ne.jp) is secured with HMAC-SHA256 request signatures, settles in JPY, sends transaction webhooks plus daily reconciliation files, and ships official Node, PHP, Python and Java SDKs under the github.com/paypay organization.

companies.name: Kyoto University
companies.description: Kyoto University is a national research university in Kyoto, Japan, ranked #37 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. Its public, machine-readable developer footprint is centered on scholarly and open-source infrastructure rather than a centralized developer portal. Confirmed public surfaces include the KURENAI research information repository (DSpace) with a live OAI-PMH metadata endpoint, the kyoto-u "Kyoto University Open Source Project" GitHub organization, and a Shibboleth/SAML integrated authentication system operated by the Institute for Information Management and Communication (IIMC). Student information, course, and timetable systems are gated behind campus accounts and are not publicly documented APIs.

The platform lets businesses create ten document types (quotes, invoices, purchase orders, receipts and more), send them electronically or by post in one click, track payments with automated bank reconciliation, and stay compliant with Japan's qualified-invoice law and electronic-bookkeeping regulations. MakeLeaps exposes a REST API at api.makeleaps.com secured with OAuth 2.0 client-credentials, letting partners create clients and documents and drive the sending workflow programmatically, plus a Salesforce (Apex) managed-package SDK and published tutorials for building your own MCP server over your invoice data.

companies.name: Kyash
companies.description: Kyash Inc. (株式会社Kyash) is a Tokyo-based fintech founded in 2015 that operates a consumer mobile wallet and Visa prepaid card in Japan, covering charging, peer-to-peer transfers, shared accounts, buy-now-pay-later, personal finance management, and contactless payment through Apple Pay, Google Pay, and Samsung Pay. Kyash is a registered Funds Transfer Service Provider (Kanto Local Finance Bureau No. 00082) and a third-party Prepaid Payment Instrument Issuer (No. 00698), and is ISO/IEC 27001:2022, PCI DSS, and TRUSTe certified. Its business-facing product is Kyash Payout, a mass payout service that sends funds to Japanese domestic bank accounts or Kyash wallets at a flat 50 yen per transfer, integrated either by Zengin/CSV file upload or by direct API integration including a balance API. Kyash previously sold Kyash Direct, an API-based Visa card issuer processing platform launched in 2019. All API access is sales-gated: Kyash publishes no developer portal, API reference, specification, SDK, or sandbox.

companies.name: Keio University
companies.description: Keio University is a private research university in Tokyo, Japan, founded in 1858, and ranked #188 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. Its public machine-readable footprint is led by KOARA (KeiO Associated Repository of Academic resources), the institutional repository, which exposes a live OAI-PMH 2.0 metadata-harvesting endpoint. Most other institutional systems (keio.jp SSO over Google Workspace, Canvas K-LMS, the K-RIS researcher system, KOSMOS library discovery, and the Keio Object Hub culture portal) are account-gated and do not publish open developer API documentation. Identity is federated through GakuNin, the Japanese academic SAML/Shibboleth federation that participates in eduGAIN.

companies.name: Nagoya University
companies.description: Nagoya University (名古屋大学) is a national research university in Nagoya, Aichi, Japan, ranked #152 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. As a leading research institution it operates a range of academic and IT services through its Information & Communications (ICTS) division and university library. Its most clearly documented public, machine-readable API surface is the NAGOYA Repository institutional repository, which runs on the NII WEKO3 / JAIRO Cloud platform and exposes an OAI-PMH 2.0 interface for harvesting scholarly metadata. Most other systems (student portal, NU-ID identity, course registration) are gated behind THERS/GakuNin (Shibboleth/SAML) authentication and are not publicly documented developer APIs.

companies.name: Waseda University
companies.description: Waseda University is a leading private research university in Tokyo, Japan, ranked #181 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. Its public, machine-readable developer footprint is centered on scholarly infrastructure rather than a dedicated developer portal: the Waseda University Repository exposes an OAI-PMH 2.0 metadata interface (hosted on the NII WEKO/JAIRO Cloud), and the library's WINE discovery service runs on the Ex Libris Primo/Alma platform (institution code 81SOKEI_WUNI), which provides standard Primo and SRU interfaces. Identity is handled via Shibboleth SAML SSO. There is no single official Waseda University GitHub organization; an unofficial student project (WasedaTime) operates a community syllabus/timetable backend that is not publicly documented.

companies.name: Tokyo Institute of Technology
companies.description: Tokyo Institute of Technology (Tokyo Tech / Titech) was a national research university in Tokyo, Japan, ranked #76 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. In October 2024 it merged with Tokyo Medical and Dental University to form the Institute of Science Tokyo (Science Tokyo), and its public web presence now lives primarily at isct.ac.jp while legacy titech.ac.jp services remain online. Its public, machine-readable developer footprint is limited: the most clearly documented programmatic interface is the T2R2 (Science Tokyo / Tokyo Tech Research Repository) OAI-PMH metadata harvesting endpoint. Identity is federated through GakuNin using Shibboleth/SAML rather than a public OAuth/OpenID Connect API. No official institution-wide REST developer portal or open-data API was found.

companies.name: University of Tokyo
companies.description: The University of Tokyo (UTokyo) is Japan's leading national research university, founded in 1877 and ranked #29 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. Its public, machine-readable developer footprint is centered on its library and digital humanities infrastructure rather than a unified developer portal. Confirmed public APIs include the UTokyo Academic Assets Archives (utda) Digital Archive Portal, which exposes IIIF-compliant image and presentation APIs plus downloadable IIIF Collections and JSON-LD/RDF metadata datasets, and the UTokyo Repository (WEKO) institutional repository, which offers an OAI-PMH 2.0 metadata harvesting endpoint. No general-purpose, authenticated REST developer program (course/SIS/timetable APIs) was found publicly documented.

companies.name: Tohoku University
companies.description: Tohoku University is a national research university in Sendai, Japan, founded in 1907 and ranked #107 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. Its public, machine-readable developer footprint is centered on scholarly infrastructure rather than a central developer portal: the TOUR (TOhoku University Repository) institutional repository runs on NII's JAIRO Cloud (WEKO3) and exposes a live OAI-PMH 2.0 endpoint for metadata harvesting. The library also operates a public OPAC. No central, self-service API developer portal, open-data platform, or SSO/OAuth client-registration program was found publicly documented; most research-code APIs live in individual lab GitHub organizations.

companies.name: Hokkaido University
companies.description: Hokkaido University (北海道大学) is a national research university in Sapporo, Japan, founded in 1876 as Sapporo Agricultural College and ranked #173 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. It operates 12 undergraduate schools, 21 graduate schools, and numerous research institutes. Its public, machine-readable developer footprint is limited and centered on scholarly infrastructure: the HUSCAP institutional repository (Hokkaido University Collection of Scholarly and Academic Papers) and public XML sitemaps. The university does not publish a dedicated developer portal or documented public REST API; most institutional systems (ELMS LMS, syllabus search, researcher directory) are web UIs without documented programmatic access.

companies.name: ANDPAD
companies.description: ANDPAD (株式会社アンドパッド / ANDPAD Inc.) is Japan's leading cloud construction-management and construction-DX platform, used by more than 260,000 companies and hundreds of thousands of field and office users across new-build housing, renovation, specialty trades, general contracting, and facilities management. The platform spans scheduling, photo and document management, drawings, inspection checklists, chat, billing, and procurement, and exposes an external REST API (api.andpad.jp) plus an app marketplace (ANDPAD App Market) so partners can integrate their own services with ANDPAD. ANDPAD is backed by Hongshan (HongShan / Sequoia China) and operates a public developer site, a system status page, and a published security.txt disclosure channel.

companies.name: NTT
companies.description: NTT (Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corporation) is a Tokyo-headquartered global technology and telecommunications group with roughly 340,000 employees and a 150-year history of innovation. The group operates through five business divisions — Consulting & IT Services, Mobile Solutions, Smart Tech, Consumer & Business, and Research & Development — and is anchored by major subsidiaries including NTT DOCOMO (Japan's largest mobile carrier), NTT Communications / NTT DOCOMO BUSINESS (enterprise cloud, network, and platform services), NTT DATA Group (global IT services and systems integration), NTT Ltd. (managed services), and NTT Research. NTT exposes a substantial developer surface through the NTT DOCOMO BUSINESS Developer Portal at developer.ntt.com, which catalogs enterprise APIs across Network (Arcstar Universal One, Flexible InterConnect, Global M2M), Cloud (Smart Data Platform, Enterprise Cloud 2.0), Voice, App (Safety Confirmation, Text & Language Analysis, Speech Recognition), Management (asset visibility, vulnerability), and Core (Authorization, Billing, API Log, Business Process, Service Order, Pay-per-use, Price, Organization, Personal Profile) categories. The group also publishes IoT APIs (Things Cloud) and a docomo Developer support portal at dev.smt.docomo.ne.jp. NTT's primary open source presence is the nttcom GitHub organization, which ships the Enterprise Cloud Python and Go SDKs (eclsdk / eclcloud), the eclcli command-line tool, Terraform providers for Enterprise Cloud 2.0 (terraform-provider- ecl) and Flexible InterConnect (terraform-provider-fic), the ksot network-IaC framework, the pola stateful PCE / PCEP library, the fluvia eBPF/XDP IPFIX exporter, and threatconnectome for SBOM-driven vulnerability management. NTT DATA additionally maintains regional GitHub orgs (NTTDATA, NTTDATA-EMEA, NTTDATA-DACH, NTTDATAInnovation, launchbynttdata, nttdata-oss) covering testing automation, Kubernetes plugins, and LLM observability tooling. NTT also drives the IOWN (Innovative Optical and Wireless Network) initiative, photonics and optical-quantum research, and responsible AI development across its R&D arm.

companies.name: Trustdock

companies.name: Souco
companies.description: Souco (株式会社souco / souco Co., Ltd.) operates a warehouse-sharing marketplace and logistics resource optimization platform in Japan, connecting cargo owners with available space across a nationwide network of 3,000+ warehouses spanning all 47 prefectures. Businesses can secure short- or long-term storage on demand for a wide range of cargo — food ingredients, apparel, machinery, and documents — under ambient, refrigerated, frozen, or temperature-controlled conditions, with pickup and delivery coordination handled by the platform. Alongside the sharing marketplace, souco offers a rental-warehouse search portal, transportation services, and the Optis engine for optimizing logistics networks, plus consulting and DX support for the logistics industry. The company is backed by 500 Global and Sumitomo Corporation's corporate venture arm. souco is a customer-facing logistics platform and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation; its digital surface is a login-gated web application at app.souco.space.

Clients describe the job they need done and receive quotes and proposals from vetted local pros, while professionals pay to respond to matched leads. Founded in 2015 and backed by 500 Global, Zehitomo runs a consumer-facing web and mobile product; it does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

companies.name: Hokan

The platform consolidates customer and policy information, digitizes proposal and activity workflows, and adds modules for intent capture (意向把握), case management (案件管理), dashboards, accounting/cashiering (出納), and staff management (People). It targets paperless operations, stronger audit and compliance controls, renewal and aftercare tracking, and mobile access for agents. Customers include Orix Life, ANA, Sekisui, and other Japanese insurers and agencies. Hokan is backed by 500 Global. The company exposes API-based website integration for its product but does not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI, or SDK; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

companies.name: Rakuten Mobile

The same engineering effort spun out into Rakuten Symphony, a B2B business that productizes the Rakuten Mobile playbook as the Symworld platform — a cloud-native operating platform for telcos covering Open RAN (CU/DU/RIC, Symware distributed unit appliance), Symworld Cloud (Kubernetes-based hyperconverged telco cloud / CNP), OSS/BSS, site management, and a marketplace of pre-integrated cloud-native network functions from 50+ vendor partners. Symphony also offers Rakuten CPaaS (carrier-grade SMS, Confirm/OTP, and Short URL APIs running on the Rakuten Mobile network with JWT-authenticated REST endpoints at api.cpaas.symphony.rakuten.net) and Rakuten Communications Platform (RCP) for enterprise private 5G. Public, developer-accessible APIs are concentrated in the CPaaS suite; the Symworld platform APIs themselves are TM Forum-aligned but exposed under commercial engagement rather than a public developer signup.

companies.name: Koska
companies.description: KOSKA Corporation (株式会社KOSKA) is a Tokyo-based manufacturing technology company, founded in October 2018, that applies cost accounting and IoT to the Japanese factory floor. Its flagship product GenKan (原価管理自動化サービス) automates cost management for high-mix low-volume manufacturers: RFID and power sensors installed on existing equipment capture work progress and consumption without changing operator behavior, then make processing cost, material cost, and electricity cost visible line by line, feeding real actual-cost figures and KPI setting back to the shop floor and management. A second product, ながら記録 (Nagara Kiroku / "vScribe"), is an AI record-keeping app for manufacturing, construction, and logistics sites — photograph a paper form and AI generates the input form, then operators record hands-free by speaking, with the AI parsing natural speech into structured records, inspections, and reports. KOSKA is led by CEO Kenichiro Sone (Forbes 30 Under 30 Asia 2021) and advised by Hiroshi Obata, former chair of the Japan Cost Accounting Association. As of this profile the company publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal — it is a sensor-and-SaaS product company, not an API provider.

companies.name: Spacee
companies.description: Spacee Inc. (株式会社スペイシー) is a Tokyo-based space-sharing and rental marketplace operator in Japan. Its consumer platforms let people discover and book temporary spaces by the hour: Yoyappin, a booking marketplace for meeting rooms, conference rooms, studios, kitchens and event venues across the Tokyo metropolitan area; THE POINT, a premium coworking and creative "third place" for remote workers; and Office Connect, a nationwide search service for shared offices, rental offices, coworking spaces and virtual offices. Spacee also expands via partnerships (e.g. JR West Japan) and acquisitions (GYYM pay-per-use fitness). It operates as a consumer web and mobile marketplace and does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

companies.name: Shippio
companies.description: Shippio is a Japanese logistics-technology company positioning itself as "Japan's first digital forwarder." It provides cloud-based SaaS for visualizing and streamlining international trade and freight-forwarding operations, combining domain expertise with AI-era digital technology. Its product line includes Shippio Forwarding (a digital forwarding service), Shippio Cargo (trade-management SaaS for shippers/importers-exporters), and Shippio Works (trade-management SaaS for logistics operators), delivered through a multi-sided platform that connects shippers and operators. The company is backed by 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass Shippio publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or pricing; its APIs are internal platform APIs referenced only in engineering job postings, so this profile is identity-only with no public API surface.

companies.name: KDDI
companies.description: KDDI Corporation is a Japanese multinational telecommunications operator headquartered in Tokyo, providing mobile, fixed-line, broadband, and enterprise ICT services. KDDI markets its consumer mobile services under the au brand, alongside UQ mobile and povo, and serves enterprise customers globally through KDDI Global and KDDI America. The company operates the KDDI Open API for Developers portal exposing inquiry-gated product APIs including the au PAY Mini App platform, an XR/MEC low-latency application API, a PPM consent management API, and an au mobile Identification Support Service for KYC/identity verification. KDDI also runs the au OPEN DEVICE DEVELOPER SITE for cellular module device certification, and a KDDI Cloud Platform Service knowledge site with developer API references for cloud infrastructure. In 2025 KDDI became an equity partner in Aduna, the GSMA/Ericsson-backed network API venture aggregating CAMARA-aligned carrier APIs (Number Verify, SIM Swap, Quality on Demand, Device Location) across global operators. Public OpenAPI specifications are not openly published; API access is provided through contact/inquiry workflows after partner onboarding.

companies.name: Ocean Network Express
companies.description: Ocean Network Express (ONE) is a Singapore-headquartered global container liner shipping company formed in 2017 through the integration of the container shipping businesses of three Japanese carriers — Nippon Yusen Kaisha (NYK), Mitsui O.S.K. Lines (MOL), and Kawasaki Kisen Kaisha (K-Line) — with commercial operations launching on 1 April 2018. Operating under the magenta "ONE" brand and the Standard Carrier Alpha Code ONEY, the company runs a fleet exceeding 2,200,000 TEU across 165+ weekly service loops calling at 244+ ports worldwide, making it one of the largest ocean container carriers globally. ONE participates in THE Alliance vessel sharing agreement and offers reefer, dangerous goods, out-of-gauge, and project cargo services alongside standard dry container moves. Its customer-facing digital surface centers on the ONE eCommerce platform (ecomm.one-line.com), which provides cargo tracking, instant quotation via ONE QUOTE (powered by Descartes Kontainers), spot booking, shipping instructions, electronic bill of lading, ePayment, and demurrage/detention inquiry. A partner-facing developer portal exists at developers.one-line.com alongside EDI integration channels, but ONE does not publish a fully open, self-service OpenAPI specification, public SDK, or open-source code at either the github.com/ocean-network-express or github.com/OceanNetworkExpress organizations (both exist with zero public repositories). Tracking, booking, and schedule integrations are most commonly accessed by shippers and BCOs through third-party aggregators (Vizion, Portcast, JSONCargo, Terminal49, Tradlinx) or via DCSA-conformant carrier APIs delivered under commercial agreement.

companies.name: Excite Japan Co., Ltd. (JASDAQ:3754)
companies.description: Excite Japan Co., Ltd. (エキサイト株式会社), listed on JASDAQ as ticker 3754, is a Tokyo-based internet media and services company founded in August 1997 and headquartered in the Azabudai Hills Mori JP Tower in Minato, Tokyo. It operates the long-running excite.co.jp web portal — offering web, image, and news search, the Excite Blog (exblog.jp) blogging platform, translation and dictionary tools, fortune-telling, recipe, and lifestyle content — alongside the BB.excite broadband/ISP business. Under parent Excite Holdings Co., Ltd., the group organizes its operations into four segments: Platform, Broadband, Medical, and SaaS/DX (including the FanGrowth customer-growth platform). The company does not currently publish a public developer API program or portal; this profile tracks its corporate and web presence within the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: Sumutasu
companies.description: Sumutasu Inc. (株式会社すむたす) is a Japanese property-technology (proptech) company operating under the mission "a society where people can make ideal housing choices" (住まいの理想的な選択ができる社会に). It runs an instant real-estate buying and selling service for used condominiums in Japan, using data and technology to give homeowners a fast, transparent alternative to the traditional brokerage process, alongside an agent-assisted sales offering. The company is backed by 500 Global. Its public presence is a corporate marketing website (About, Services, Members, News, and Careers) built on the Studio.Design no-code platform; no public developer platform, API, SDK, or documentation surface has been found.

companies.name: Dverse
companies.description: Dverse is the API Evangelist network profile for Symmetry Dimensions Inc. (株式会社SYMMETRY), a Tokyo-based technology company whose "DVERSE" digital-twin lineage evolved into a portfolio of DX solution services, infrastructure operations and maintenance support (インフラ維持管理支援), and SDTC data services. The company was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the network as an enrichment lead. The branded domain symmetry-dimensions.com now redirects to the company's live site at symmetry-inc.co.jp. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a corporate/marketing site (a Nuxt single-page app on Google Cloud) but no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDK, CLI, MCP server, or /.well-known discovery surface — so no machine-readable API artifacts could be harvested. This record therefore carries company identity plus a probed domain-security profile only, and remains a lead awaiting a public API surface.

companies.name: HiCustomer
companies.description: HiCustomer (ハイカスタマー) was a Japanese Customer Success Management (CSM) SaaS built specifically for SaaS companies. Its platform aggregated customer data scattered across BI tools, CRMs, and chat tools to visualize product usage, communication history, revenue, and contract information in one place. Teams used configurable health-score rules to monitor account health across the customer lifecycle, and custom alerts to surface churn and upsell signals at the right moment, with time-series analysis to make customer-success outreach repeatable. The company also offered customer-success consulting. As of this enrichment pass the hicustomer.jp domain no longer resolves to a live site (its authoritative AWS Route 53 zone is empty) and the product appears discontinued; the last archived homepage (Oct 2024) shows only a minimal "About the company" page. No public developer API, documentation, SDK, or developer portal was ever published.

companies.name: SODA
companies.description: SODA Inc. (株式会社SODA) is a Japanese consumer-technology company that operates SNKRDUNK (スニーカーダンク / スニダン), one of Japan's largest consumer-to-consumer marketplaces for sneakers, trading cards ("トレカ"), apparel, and accessories. The SNKRDUNK app lets users buy and sell collectible and secondary-market goods with professional in-house authentication (真贋鑑定 by プロ鑑定士) and a full purchase-protection / compensation guarantee, alongside a buyback service. SODA is a portfolio company of the SoftBank Vision Fund. As a consumer marketplace app, SODA publishes no public developer program or API at this time; this profile captures the company's public identity and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

companies.name: DCM Ventures
companies.description: DCM Ventures (formerly Doll Capital Management, and commonly known as DCM) is an early-stage venture capital firm founded in 1996 by Dixon Doll, a former Accel partner, and David Chao, and headquartered at 2420 Sand Hill Road in Menlo Park, California with additional offices in Beijing and Tokyo. DCM was among the first Silicon Valley firms to build a cross-border, US-Asia investing practice, and typically leads early-stage rounds with checks in the roughly $1M-$5M range, deploying capital into a small group of category-defining companies each year rather than investing broadly. The firm's thesis has evolved from its original focus on communications and semiconductors toward consumer internet and SaaS, and today centers on vertical SaaS, fintech, cross-border innovation, and AI-native applications across the United States, China, Japan, and Southeast Asia. As of 2025 DCM manages approximately $4.5 billion in assets and reports 400+ portfolio companies, 35+ unicorns, and over $150 billion in aggregate market value, with notable investments including SoFi, Bill.com, Kuaishou, Matterport, 51job, Careem, and Sansan.
